newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says MGAM incident "isolated" - papers.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says MGAM incident "isolated" - papers.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG told German newspapers on Friday the crisis at its London fund management arm MGAM was an isolated one and questioned whether MGAM's investment philosophy suited its parent.

While acknowledging that its supervision methods had failed, Deutsche board members accused fund manager Peter Young, one of the two fund managers at the centre of the MGAM crisis, of deceiving his superiors.

"We are pushing for susbstantial improvements in internal controls. In addition we will have to review whether MGAM's investment philosophy suits Deutsche Bank's rather more conservative overall concept," Deutsche board member Rolf Breuer told the daily Handelsblatt on Friday.
Breuer, who has overall responsibilty for Deutsche's asset management worldwide, added: "Funds are better controlled in Germany. Something like this is not possible here."

In a separate interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Breuer said: "This was an isolated incident involving two fund managers and cannot be extended to Deutsche Bank's whole fund business."
Trading in three MGAM funds were suspended this week pending a probe into alleged irregularities by fund manager Peter Young. A colleague, Stewart Armer, was suspended on Wednesday evening.
Deutsche has spent 180 million pounds ($282 million) to buy up the unlisted securities which formed the dubious content of the funds for its own account.

Michael Dobson, fellow Deutsche board member and head of Deutsche's investment banking arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told Handelsblatt that Peter Young "appeared to have blinded" his superiors to his activities.
In an interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, he said Young had "deceived his superiors" when he was advised to reduce its investments in unlisted companies in April.
"As head of the investment bank I take responsibility for the events...our internal controls failed," Dobson, to whom MGAM reports, said.
The newspaper noted, however, that Dobson faced no personal consequences from the MGAM saga.
The London Financial Times on Friday cited Breuer as saying Deutsche was considering shifting control of MGAM's unit trust business to Frankfurt from London.
Deutsche declined comment on the report, but has already said it is reviewing its internal controls in the light of this week's events. ($ = 0.638 British Pounds Sterling)
